title.narrative: COVID-19: Second Shock-Responsive Social Protection Project

description.narrative: With a worsening coronavirus disease (COVID-19) situation unfolding in the fourth quarter of 2020, the Government of Mongolia has requested urgent additional support for social protection measures to mitigate the socioeconomic impacts of the pandemic on poor and vulnerable groups. The proposed project will (i) apply shock-responsive social protection principles to continue support for pro-poor child grant top-ups on a temporary basis through an established national social assistance program, and (ii) strengthen social welfare programs and systems for improved household resilience and government response to future crises.

description.narrative: Output/s as listed by the project staff.

Output: Social welfare programs and systems strengthened Indicator: At least 1,500 working-age adults in poor households (50% women) receive graduation program asset packages with coaching and training to promote diversified income sources (2020 baseline: 0 households) Achievement: 1259 Progress/Status: Completed. At the launch of the MGPP, a total of 1,520 households were randomly selected from 3,035 eligible households and received initial orientation and training. However, 261 households dropped out due to various reasons such as refusal to participate, lack of a qualified main participant, relocation, or other household circumstances.
As a result, 1,259 households-83% of those initially selected-continue to participate in the MGPP: 716 in Songinokhairkhan district, 336 in Bayanzurkh district, and 207 in Chingeltei district. Among them, three households have not selected livelihood options, but participated in savings groups and other activities. Women have been the main participants in 916 households (72.8%), and 475 households (37.7%) have been female-headed.
In total, the MGPP benefitted 7,402 individuals, including family members. Among them, 2,617 (35%) are women; 3,430 are working-age adults, 3,422 are children, of whom 1,232 (36%) are girls. Also, although the number of households participating is below 1,500, in many of them, livelihood activities, such as vegetable cultivation and food processing, are supported by more than one adult member of the household. Out of the beneficiaries, 99.9% (913 women,72,7%) received asset packages for their livelihood businesses.
By the end of the MGPP in June 2025, a total duplicated number of 16,908 adults (including 12,258 women, representing 72.5) have engaged in various trainings, including those on life skills, business and technical skills, financial education, and social empowerment.
A total of 7402 members of 1,259 beneficiary households received coaching and mentoring every month during the implementation of the MGPP. Data Source: Project quarterly reports

Output: Social welfare programs and systems strengthened Indicator: At least 14 additional social welfare programs are connected to the "e-welfare" system (2020 baseline: 5 programs) Achievement: 64 Progress/Status: Completed. This target has been met, with 64 welfare services out of a total of 72 connected to the government integrated social welfare system 'e-halamj'. Sixty-four welfare services are now available on the e-welfare system, compared to a baseline of only 5 programs in 2020 and 14 additional social welfare programs that were to be digitalized under the project.
The 'e-halamj' system is developed by the IT Center for Customs, Taxation and Finance, a state-owned enterprise, while GOLWS provides support to its development, system administration, and database management.
A total of four IT consultants provided technical support to GOLWS by (i) developing a reporting system for social welfare services, (ii) developing a web-based dashboard showing data on the expenditure of the welfare fund, (iii) identifying paper-based documents that are still required for welfare services and digitizing them, (iv) restructuring and improving servers and related hardware of GOLWS, (v) installing and setting up a database server (Exadata) at the National Data Center that will be used to store data of the “e-welfare” system, (vi) developing terms of reference for a financial system, and (vii) providing other technical support from 2022 to 2024.
64 welfare services are now available on the e-welfare system compared to 14 additional social welfare programs that were to be digitalized under the project, and there were only 5 programs available on the e-welfare system in 2020. 2 IT consultants who worked on the improvement of the Business Intelligence (BI) system for MFLSP had 2 person-months each left for upgrading software licenses to newer versions. However, the EA decided to suspend the remaining inputs of 2 person-months due to the MOF's restriction to postpone the financing of these consulting services until 2026. Data Source: "E-welfare" system reports

Output: Social welfare programs and systems strengthened Indicator: Proxy means test data for at least 26,900 households those with the lowest scores and those that receive the food stamp are recertified using new methodology through household visits, with data disaggregated by age, sex, and geographic area Achievement: 25768 Progress/Status: The output performance indicator has been achieved. Based on the approved PMT methodology, a survey to re-certify households was conducted nationwide in May-June 2023. The project supported GOLWS to visit and survey 27,274 households who were mostly beneficiaries of the Food Stamp Program (FSP). The administrative data for these households were retrieved electronically from six government agencies; however, the data exchange was delayed due to the time required to establish web services for data exchange between government entities. The collected survey data, disaggregated by age, sex, and geographic area, have been entered into the updated database. Retrieval and cleaning of data for 135,831 people from 27,274 households from six government agencies, and integration into the household database, were carried out from June 2023 to March 2024. Based on all the collected data, the household scores have been calculated using the revised PMT methodology.
However, due to inconsistencies between the information obtained from the administrative data and the households visits, the MFLSP and GOLWS decided to visit and survey an additional number of households. In August-November 2024, GOLWS visited and surveyed over 30,000 households currently benefiting from the Food Stamp Program (FSP) to verify the accuracy of the household scores. In addition, GOLWS continues to retrieve the administrative data for all households in the country from nine government agencies, which currently stands at 60%. Once all the data collected are integrated into the IHD, all the household scores will be calculated using the PMT software. After the IHD is updated, the MFLSP and GOLWS will be able to determine beneficiaries of targeted social welfare programs such as the FSP by assigning eligibility thresholds in line with the allocated budget. Thus, it is expected that the IHD will be fully updated by August 2025.
Data Source: GOLWS reports generated from the IHD

Output: Pro-poor child grant top-ups delivered Indicator: Child grant monthly benefit level topped-up to MNT100,000 per child for 12 additional months, January-December 2021 (March 2020 pre-COVID-19 baseline: regular child grant benefit of MNT20,000 per month) Achievement: 100000 Progress/Status: Exceeded. This output has been completed, achieving the performance indicator of topping up the child grant monthly benefit to MNT100,000 per child for 7 months (January to June and December 2021, as agreed during the inception mission). The total number of children increased from 1,190,283 in January to 1,208,411 in June, and 1,220,158 in December 2021, marking a 3.04% increase over the November 2020 baseline of 1,184,158. On average, girls comprised 48.9% of the total. Data Source: Approved 2021 government budget
Social welfare support for the poor and vulnerable, especially women and children, enhanced

At least 80% of graduation pilot program beneficiaries (50% women) have improved livelihoods as measured by the graduation criteria established under the pilot program Achievement: 80 Progress/Status: Completed. The Mongolian Graduation Pilot Program (MGPP) was implemented from June 2022 to June 2025 to improve the livelihoods of targeted households by promoting economic inclusion, income diversification, and poverty reduction.
A total of 1,259 households of the selected three districts of capital Ulaanbaatar City - 83% of those initially selected - participated in the MGPP: 716 in Songinokhairkhan district, 336 in Bayanzurkh district, and 207 in Chingeltei district. Among them, three households have not selected livelihood options, but participated in savings groups and other activities. Women have been the main participants in 916 households (72.8%), and 475 households (37.7%) have been female-headed.
The graduation criteria have been developed across the four graduation pillars to determine if the households have made sufficient progress to “graduate out of poverty”. The beneficiaries' progress was monitored every quarter throughout the MGPP and measured using the 11 graduation indicators at the end of the MGPP implementation.
As of 30 June 2025, a total of 1015 beneficiaries (80.6% of total beneficiaries), of which 737 women (58.5% women), have improved their livelihoods as measured by graduation criteria. Data Source: Impact evaluation end line survey report, 2023

At least 1.2 million children nationwide (at least 48.2% girls)b registered in the IHD receive topped-up child grant benefits (November 2020 baseline: 1,184,158 children [613,517 boys and 570,641 (48.2%) girls]) Achievement: 1220158 Progress/Status: Exceeded. The project supported 7 months of topped-up child grant benefits (January to June and December 2021). The total number of children increased from 1,190,283 in January to 1,208,411 in June and 1,220,158 in December 2022 (source: General Office of Labor and Social Welfare reimbursement claims). On average, girls comprised 48.9% of the total. Data Source: GOLWS reports generated from the IHD
